# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have communicated the manual only through gestures, so Deaf must identify the key marked ᘔ, press it first, observe the resulting light, and tell Blind which wire color to cut according to the manual’s mapping. Since I cannot speak or touch the bomb, I am sending Deaf an ordered press-and-relay gesture sequence.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👇", "🫵", "👉"])
```

TURN 2

Press the key that wears ᘔ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please relay to deaf, using any agreed gesture code, a complete description of the display, light, keypad labels and entry state, and all wire colours and markings. Also tell me the manual's exact rules for choosing keys and cutting wires.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0, yellow light, keypad requires 1 digit and is empty. Key 1 has a zigzag-like printed glyph; key 2 has a circular or spiral-like glyph; key 3 has a branched angular glyph; key 4 has an angular glyph like a rotated T. Wires left to right are red, yellow, green. Please consult the manual and state the exact digit and physical action for Blind.

The glyph on key 1 is the zigzag-like mark matching ᘔ, so Blind must press key 1 first. The light is yellow, which means the yellow wire must be cut. I am using gestures to tell Deaf: key 1, press it, then select the middle wire; Deaf should relay the complete instruction aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👇", "✌"])
```

(empty)

The required sequence remains: press key 1, whose glyph matches ᘔ, before any other bomb contact; the yellow light then requires cutting the yellow wire, which is the middle wire. I am repeating the gesture code to Deaf so it can be relayed to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👇", "✌"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Please gesture the exact manual rule again, including whether it specifies a key position, a wire position, or an order of actions. Use one gesture sequence for each item, with pauses between items.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤲 🫵 🖐]
Deaf says to Mute: Blind gestured: two open upward-facing hands, pointing at the recipient, then a raised open hand. Exact symbols: 🤲 🫵 🖐. Please interpret this with the manual and send the exact keypad action to Blind.

The manual specifies an order of actions: first press the key in the key position bearing ᘔ; only after that, use the resulting light to choose a wire by color. Here the matching key is position 1, and the yellow light selects the yellow wire, which is the middle wire. Using our agreed code, I am sending Deaf the three items separately: key position 1, press, and middle wire.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇"])
wait()
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

The safe action is unchanged: key position 1 bears the ᘔ-like zigzag glyph, and it must be pressed first. The yellow light then requires cutting the yellow wire, which is the middle wire. I am repeating the agreed code to Deaf, with pauses between the required steps; Deaf can verbally provide Blind the four glyph descriptions he can see.

```

wait()
```

The manual requires key position 1 first, followed by the yellow wire, which is wire position 2 from the left. I will send Deaf two separate gesture messages so the groups can be counted unambiguously and relayed plainly to Blind.


Blind says to Mute: Do not repeat the three manual gestures. Encode the required key as N repetitions of thumbs-up, then one OK sign as separator, then the required wire as N repetitions of thumbs-down, then a handshake. Deaf must count and report both numbers. If no wire is required, send zero thumbs-down.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤲 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖]
Deaf says to Mute: Blind's latest exact sequence is 🤲 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖: two open upward-facing hands, upward-pointing finger, V sign, I-love-you hand, and crossed-fingers/raised-fingers hand. Please interpret it with the manual and give Blind the exact safe action.

The required key is position 1, and after pressing it the yellow light requires wire position 2. I will encode those numbers exactly as requested: one thumbs-up, an OK separator, two thumbs-down, then a handshake.

